about:
Castellano Custom Furniture operates from a workshop and showroom on North Columbia Boulevard in Portland, Oregon. The company was founded more than 40 years ago as a family venture and remains three generations strong, though the exact founding year and founders' names are not publicly disclosed.

The firm manufactures custom upholstered furniture—sofas, sectionals, loveseats, chairs, and ottomans—entirely in its Portland facility. It offers a full design-to-build service: consultation, collaborative design, and handcrafted production using locally sourced alder frames, domestically produced foam, recycled steel springs, and eco-friendly textiles. The operation also maintains a curated pre-made collection. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

Primary customers are residential buyers and interior designers, the latter served through a dedicated designer portal. The company sells directly to homeowners and also works with design professionals on custom projects. No specific commercial or institutional clients are named.

Castellano emphasizes sustainability and durability as differentiators: waste-free manufacturing that recycles sawdust into heating fuel and foam scraps into carpet padding, lifetime warranties on frames and springs, and a commitment to biodegradable or recyclable materials. The business was started on the belief that every piece should be as unique as the person designing it.

name: Catalyst Communications
old_description: A modern dispatch console system optimized for mission critical communications requirements of Public Safety, Utility, Education, and Transportation agencies.
about:
Catalyst Communications was founded in 1997 in Forest, Virginia, a community in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains near Lynchburg. The company emerged as a provider of Radio Control over IP solutions for critical communications agencies.

The firm develops its own dispatch console system, Propulsion™, a transportable communications tool called ICE™, and an interoperability platform named IntelliLink that bridges land mobile radio and LTE networks. Its engineering focus spans software development, IP network optimization, and standards-based interfaces for P25, DMR, and mission-critical push-to-talk over cellular. With over 25 years in the market, Catalyst supports agencies nationwide from its Virginia headquarters.

Customers include public safety, utility, education, transportation, and government organizations. Concrete references cite the Florida Highway Patrol, Federal Land Management Agencies, Honolulu public safety agencies, the Dallas Georgia Police Department, a county public safety district, an electric cooperative, and a state forestry commission. The company also partners with FirstNet and Southern Linc to extend its interoperability reach.

Catalyst says its differentiation rests on being first to market with Radio Control over IP technology, holding licenses with numerous radio manufacturers for advanced digital control, and developing the P25 CSSI/DFSI, DMR AIS, and 3GPP MCPTT interfaces. It also emphasizes 24/7 customer support as a core commitment.

old_description: SYSTEM DESIGN EQUIPMENT SALES INSTALLATIONS REPAIRS MARINE NAVIGATION COMMUNICATION AUDIO/VIDEO COMPUTER NETWORKING ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS
about:
Cay Electronics is based in Portsmouth, Rhode Island, and has been providing marine systems engineering services for over 40 years. The company serves clients throughout New England and worldwide, including boat owners, builders, shipyards, captains, and crew.

The firm offers a full range of marine electronics and electrical services: system design, equipment sales and wholesale distribution, installation, commissioning, consulting, and repair. As authorized dealers for marine manufacturers, they supply navigation, communication, audio/video, networking, and electrical power systems. Certified technicians follow in-house installation standards, and the company maintains a large inventory for same-day shipping worldwide.

Cay Electronics works with recreational and commercial marine customers, from trailer boats to superyachts and workboat fleets. Their projects cover navigation and charting, autopilot, radar, sonar, satellite communications (including Starlink and Iridium), battery systems (gel, AGM, lithium), electric propulsion, solar installations, digital switching, and CCTV.

The company emphasizes detailed system drawings that auto-generate bills of materials and wire lists, simplifying installation and future service. Their approach combines expert product selection to maximize performance and budget with thorough commissioning that includes firmware updates, sea trials, and hands-on instruction.

name: Central Electric Cooperative
old_description: View your energy usage and demand. Make payments and manage your account.
about:
Central Electric Cooperative is a member-owned, not-for-profit electric utility headquartered in Mitchell, South Dakota. While its exact founding year is not publicly stated in available materials, the cooperative has long served rural communities in the region with electricity and related energy services.

The cooperative provides electric distribution across its service territory and operates a member-facing platform called SmartHub for energy usage monitoring, bill payment, and service requests. Beyond power delivery, it runs a full-service department offering appliance sales and repair, heating and cooling installation and maintenance (including heat pumps and mini-splits), and electrical wiring for both agricultural and residential customers. Additional offerings include generator sales, solar well pump installation, and a distributed energy application process for members pursuing renewable generation. A dedicated Betts Road Service Center supports these hands-on services.

Central Electric serves residential, agricultural, and commercial members within its territory. Concrete examples from its programs include rebates for energy-efficient heat pumps and water heaters, youth scholarships and leadership tours, and the Operation Round-Up program that rounds up member bills to fund community grants. The cooperative also assists members with distributed energy interconnection and load management.

The cooperative model itself is the primary differentiator: as a not-for-profit, margins are returned to members as capital credits. The organization emphasizes local governance, community reinvestment through grants and safety education, and a service-first approach summarized in its messaging about why cooperatives still matter.

Central Florida Metal Shop, doing business as Central Florida Metals, operates from Orlando, Florida. The company’s website has carried a 2021 copyright notice, indicating it was established by that year; no founders or ownership structure are disclosed in public sources.

The shop specializes in sheet metal fabrication, welding, and duct metal fabrication, producing commercial ductwork ancillary components for HVAC and construction projects. Its capabilities also extend to construction-related services such as general contracting, design-build, pre-construction, pre-fabrication, and 24-hour maintenance, according to its services page. The company serves the commercial construction sector, including apartment, villa, and industrial building projects, as well as the broader metal fabrication industry. Its ductwork components are used in HVAC systems for new construction and renovation work.

The firm emphasizes a “Metal Fabrication Done Right!” approach and highlights a three-step philosophy built on people, process, and partnership, with services that extend to design-build, pre-construction, and pre-fabrication support.

about:
Central Kentucky Industrial, Inc. operates from Richmond, Kentucky, where it runs a full-service fabrication shop and provides industrial contracting services. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company specializes in dust, fume, and mist collection solutions for major industries. Its fabrication shop produces ductwork and system components such as support stands, platforms, ladders, handrails, conveyors, machine guards, chutes, down-draft tables, and containment booths. Capabilities include sheet metal fabrication, structural steel fabrication, all-type welding (working with PVC, stainless steel, mild steel, structural steel, and special steel), and on-site installation services for equipment moves, repairs, and new installations.

Central Kentucky Industrial serves clients across sectors requiring dust and fume control, with a customer list that includes Corning, Superior Battery, Sherwin Williams, Firestone, Bondtech, EnerSys, GE, TG Kentucky, TTAI Corporation, Novelis Aluminum, and BGCAPP.

The company states its mission is to listen to client needs and deliver custom products within agreed timelines, provide quality workmanship within economical means, and never sacrifice safety, quality, or integrity. It also emphasizes exceptional customer service, employee development, and respect for all staff as professionals.

name: Central Wire Industries
old_description: Specialty/precision wire manufacturing (AS9100 certified facility; HQ is Canada-based)
about:
Central Wire Industries operates from Perris, California, and traces its roots to 1955 when it began producing fine-diameter red-metal wire for fourdrinier fabric used in paper manufacturing. The company later expanded into stainless-steel fine wire and grew through acquisitions across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. As of August 2026, the Central Wire Group of Companies is owned by Altair Industries, a private-equity firm focused on aerospace, defense, and mission-critical industrial businesses.

The company manufactures a broad line of specialty wire products including bar stock, cold-heading wire, fine and ultra-fine wire, knitted wire mesh, resistance wire, shaped and profiled wire, slicklines, spring wire, and welding wire. Processes cover rod processing, breakdown drawing, centerless grinding, custom profiling, knitting, and both destructive and non-destructive testing. With 11 locations in three countries and more than 750 employees, Central Wire serves both mission-critical and commercial markets.

Customers span aerospace, architecture, automotive, medical, military and defense, oil and gas, and food and beverage industries. Products are used in mission-critical fastening systems, heating coils for appliances and flooring, downhole slicklines for sour and sweet environments, and welding consumables for MIG, TIG, and submerged-arc processes.

Central Wire states that its differentiation lies in the widest range of high-performance specialty alloys — nickel, stainless, and red metals — combined with global reach, DFARS-compliant materials, and a focus on adaptable, premium-quality products delivered through innovative and eco-friendly manufacturing practices.

about:
Century Sheet Metal operates from Warwick, Rhode Island, where it has served Southern New England for nearly five decades. The company was founded by Charles Patterson Jr. on a mission to deliver quality work and honest service, and it remains a family-owned business now in its third generation under the leadership of President Chaz Patterson and Vice President Chelsea Kwolek.

The shop provides HVAC duct system design, fabrication, and installation from its facility Unit B. Its in-house fabrication capability allows custom ductwork to be built to precise specifications for residential, commercial, and industrial projects, with a focus on air-tight, durable systems.

Customers range from homeowners and local businesses to industrial facilities across Rhode Island and Massachusetts. The company tailors each project to the building’s unique airflow requirements, whether for new construction or retrofit applications.

Century Sheet Metal emphasizes a hands-on, customized approach backed by three generations of craftsmanship. The current leadership aims to modernize operations while preserving the company’s commitment to prompt, professional service and on-time delivery.

name: CenturyLink
old_description: when you switch to a CenturyLink Fiber Internet plan with speeds of 200 Mbps or greater
about:
CenturyLink operates from Sioux Falls, South Dakota, providing telecommunications services across residential, small business, and enterprise segments. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed in the available materials, though it operates under the Lumen Technologies umbrella as indicated by corporate branding.

The company delivers fiber-optic internet service with speeds up to 940 Mbps, alongside traditional TV and landline phone offerings. Service tiers include plans supporting 20+ connected devices, marketed for smart homes, competitive gaming, and multi-user households. CenturyLink leases WiFi equipment and provides a mobile application for network management, parental controls, and cybersecurity features. Professional installation is included with fiber orders.

Customers span individual households, small businesses, and enterprise accounts. The service is positioned for work-from-home connectivity, streaming, gaming, and smart-home integration. A referral program offers financial incentives for customer acquisition, and a moving service facilitates transfer of existing accounts to new addresses.

CenturyLink emphasizes month-to-month agreements without annual contracts or early-termination fees, transparent pricing, and a no-credit-check prepay option. Free professional installation on fiber plans is highlighted as a differentiator, along with a referral program that includes charitable donations.

name: Cerrowire
old_description: Take our 3-question EfficiencyMax Test to see if you’re using the right material for the job. Don’t let a bad pull ruin your day.
about:
Headquartered in Hartselle, Alabama, Cerrowire operates as a subsidiary of Marmon/Berkshire Hathaway. The company manufactures copper and aluminum building wire and cable at plants in Alabama, Georgia, Indiana, and Utah, including a new state-of-the-art MC cable facility. Founding year and founders are not publicly disclosed.

Cerrowire produces a range of electrical wire and cable products: building wire (THHN, NM-B), MC cables, portable cord, and specialty wires. Its manufacturing capabilities include special cuts, paralleling, and single-use pulling grips. The company also offers value-added services such as a prepaid freight return program, warranty coverage, and a copper scrap return program. Innovations like the ReelRover wire handling device, tangle-free CerroPack packaging, an exterior coding system on MC cables, and CerroMax color-coded NM-B cables aim to reduce installation time and errors.

The company serves commercial, industrial, and residential construction markets across North America. Its customers include electrical contractors, builders, electricians, and large-scale construction firms. Products reach end users through a nationwide network of electrical distributors, wholesalers, and retail partners.

Cerrowire emphasizes continuous improvement through an 80/20 process that drives efficiency across its plants. The company states its focus on innovation in wire design, advanced packaging, and streamlined distribution provides competitive advantages, with products that exceed industry standards and tools that improve jobsite productivity.
